measures.what: Fund seven-day discharge coordination, transitional and rehab capacity and targeted home support, and close surge and overflow beds (especially agency-staffed ones) as ALC falls, so the saving is real; 50% of the saving after replacement care goes to home care. Home care is funded from recurring health and SLTC savings (P1-P4 and this measure), not from LTC amortization or facility-delay timing, and is budgeted at its real level (E5).
measures.basis: CIHI, 2023-24: 21.3% of NS hospital days were ALC (192K days) vs 16.9% nationally. Derived: about 901K total days; reaching the national rate with total days unchanged means about 40K fewer ALC days a year (192K x 4.4/21.3 = 39.7K; 47.7K if avoided days also leave the total). measures.name: Over-budget spending: offsets first, Finance's own commitments delivered, then the Canadian norm
measures.what: Start with what Finance already accepted: the Grants Management Framework review and OAG Rec 1.5 terms (E6). No discretionary grants by additional appropriation in the last quarter without documented immediate need; publish order-in-council detail with each forecast update; and have the House vote on additional appropriations above a small threshold at its next sitting, as in the other nine provinces and Ottawa. Unused contingency lapses to deficit reduction. If the House prefers a larger voted contingency in place of open-ended top-ups, it is shown below the line and any unused amount lapses, so the published deficit does not rise.

measures.name: Make the 40% net-debt guardrail real: a legislated glide path, a capital plan paced to it, and a correction plan (not automatic cuts)
measures.what: Legislate the government's own 'under 40%' net debt-to-GDP guardrail with a published glide path back below it; a published correction plan if the path is breached, not automatic cuts; an annual Auditor General report on progress; and a published comparison of program-expense growth with nominal GDP growth each year (a benchmark, not a statutory cap). Publish the 2027-28 to 2029-30 capital plan by category and pace it to the glide path (A4).
measures.basis: $0 directly. The plan breaches 40% in every year (42.8%, 45.0%, 46.0%), and even the government's own no-LTC-change line passes 40% from 2028-29 (40.9% before contingency; about 41.1% after). With this plan and the A4 capital deferral, net debt is still about $4.4B above 40% of GDP in 2029-30 (final-debt-check.py). Net capital additions (about $1.2-2.3B a year in the plan) drive net debt more than deficits do, so operating restraint alone cannot meet the guardrail within the horizon; on an illustrative path the ratio falls below 40% only in the late 2030s at a lower capital pace, and in the 2040s at the plan's 2029-30 pace.
